key_insight: Hybrid Reasoning Agents combine hidden latent reasoning with visible text-based interaction, letting an agent think efficiently internally while still using tools and communicating with the environment. This creates a single system that can switch between private reasoning and external action when needed.
problem_solved: Current LLM agents are forced to do both reasoning and interaction in text, which is inefficient and limits reasoning depth. Latent reasoning is more efficient but usually cannot access tools or provide transparent, controllable actions.
method: Use a unified generation process that dynamically switches between latent reasoning and text output.
Keep internal reasoning in a compact latent space for efficiency, then convert to text when the agent needs to act or interact externally.
Enable seamless movement between private thought and observable action so the agent can reason deeply without losing tool access or transparency.
impact: This approach can make AI agents more capable, efficient, and adaptable for real-world tasks that need both deep reasoning and external interaction. For practitioners, it offers a promising path to reduce token waste while preserving usability and control.
